## Faster record retrieval

This release improves retrieval performance, particularly when fetching many
records distributed across a large FASTA file.

- Avoid cloning complete decoded index blocks during cached lookups.
- Add opt-in parallel record retrieval with `--fetch-threads <N>`.
- Preserve query order when fetching records in parallel.
- Keep regular-expression-only retrieval sequential and streaming.
- Document parallel-fetch usage.

Testing with a 2 GiB BGZF FASTA with 1,000 distributed queries (i.e. non-adjacent records), sequential
retrieval was about 2.3 times faster and retrieval with 16 workers was about
5.9 times faster. Index creation performance and index contents were unchanged.

Example:

```bash
fastars fetch \
  --fasta sequences.fna.bgz \
  --ids-file ids.txt \
  --fetch-threads 8
```

Parallel fetching is opt-in, and the default remains one fetch worker, so no breaking changes on `fastars` usage. Also, existing `.ffx` indexes remain compatible.
